8.NGS Data AnalysisSequencing data analysis is done in two steps. In the first step we process raw reads, from which the peptide sequences are inferred. In the second step we process the peptide sequences to generate a nonredundant peptide sequence dataset. The reason for the second step is the following: If a gPhage display library has high coverage, several slightly different peptides that correspond to the same epitope may be recovered. In general, it means that peptide sequence clustering is necessary to generate a nonredundant epitope/antigen sequence dataset. steps.title: Grow T. cruzi epimastigotes
steps.instruction: Culture T. cruzi epimastigotes at 28 °C in LIT medium supplemented with 10 % heat‑inactivated cell‑culture‑grade fetal bovine serum until the culture reaches ~10⁹ cells mL⁻¹ (approximately 1 week, depending on strain).

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 200 mL of saturated culture at 1,000 × g, 23–25 °C for 10 min, discard supernatant and wash the pellet three times with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS).

steps.title: Lyse cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 20 mL lysis buffer containing 1 % SDS and proteinase K at 100 µg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Incubate lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate the suspension at 50 °C for 2 h, then centrifuge and retain the supernatant.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (1:1 vol/vol) of phenol:chloroform, vortex to homogenize, and centrifuge 5 min at 7,000 × g, 23–25 °C. Repeat the extraction until no solid material is visible at the interface, then carefully recover the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: To the aqueous phase add 0.1 vol of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 2 vol of ice‑cold ethanol, mix and incubate at –20 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Collect and wash DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, wash the pellet with 70 % ethanol, and gently resuspend in 2 mL TE buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA). Note: ~2 mg of genomic DNA is typically obtained for a library of ~10⁸ transformants.

steps.title: Select and pool serum samples
steps.instruction: Choose donor serum according to study criteria (e.g., ≥2 positive anti‑T. cruzi tests, ECG/Echo classification) and pool samples into cohorts of 10 donors each, creating two independent biological duplicates for each condition: control (2 × 10), asymptomatic (2 × 10), mild cardiomyopathy (2 × 10), severe cardiomyopathy (2 × 10).

steps.title: Purify IgG from pools
steps.instruction: Purify IgG from each pooled serum using Protein‑G Sepharose (GE Healthcare) following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Assess IgG quality
steps.instruction: Check purified IgG by SDS‑PAGE, quantify concentration with Bradford (or equivalent) aiming for 50–100 µg mL⁻¹ and purity >90 %; aliquot and store at ≤ –20 °C until use.

steps.title: First PCR for sequencing library
steps.instruction: Set up a  PCR using 10 ng plasmid DNA (from naïve or selected library) with all eight primers (4 forward, 4 reverse) listed in Table 3, a high‑fidelity polymerase (e.g., NEB Q5 or Roche KAPA HiFi), and run: 95 °C × 3 min; 20 cycles of 98 °C × 15 s, 58 °C × 15 s, 72 °C × 45 s; final 72 °C × 2 min; hold at 12 °C.

steps.title: Purify first‑PCR product
steps.instruction: Clean the amplicon with a silica‑column kit (e.g., QIAquick PCR Purification Kit).

steps.title: Second PCR for indexing
steps.instruction: Perform a second PCR with Nextera XT (Illumina) primers to add indices using KAPA HiFi: 95 °C × 3 min; 8 cycles of 98 °C × 15 s, 55 °C × 15 s, 72 °C × 45 s; final 72 °C × 2 min; hold at 12 °C. Follow the Nextera XT kit protocol, quantify the library by qPCR (Kapa Biosystems Library Quantification Kit) and dilute to a final concentration of 4 nM.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Load the 4 nM library onto an Illumina MiSeq using the MiSeq Reagent Kit v2 (500 cycles). Alternative platforms (e.g., NovaSeq SP 2 × 250 cycles) may be used; adjust read length (e.g., 2 × 150 bp) as needed, noting longer reads capture longer inserts but reduce throughput.

steps.title: Assemble paired‑end reads
steps.instruction: Assemble raw paired‑end reads with PEAR (or FastP/PandaSeq) to generate merged FastQ files.

steps.title: Process reads with dna_processing.py
steps.instruction: Install Python 3 with pandas v1.3.0, biopython v1.79, numpy v1.21.0; ensure local BlastN/BlastP are installed. Create BlastN and BlastP databases for the reference genome and proteome, edit dna_processing.py variables (BLASTN_EXE, BLASTN_DB, BLASTP_EXE, BLASTP_DB, dict_sample_fastq, cutoff_dna_identity = 0.9, cutoff_peptide_similarity = 0.6, option_remove_singletons, option_remove_DNA_below_the_arbitrary_cutoff, option_remove_peptide_below_cutoff). Run `python3 dna_processing.py` to produce output tables (dna_dataframe.xlsx, dna_above_cutoff.xlsx, dna_below_cutoff.xlsx, peptide_dataframe.xlsx, norm_peptide_df.xlsx, peptide_above_cutoff.xlsx, peptide_below_cutoff.xlsx, statistics.xlsx, peptides.txt).

steps.title: Cluster peptide sequences
steps.instruction: Install Python 3 with biopython and fuzzywuzzy (Levenshtein), and install MAFFT and HMMER. Edit clustering.py variables (PEPTIDES_TXT, MAFFT, HMMBUILD, HMMEMIT, K = 4, min_len = 6, score_cutoff = 80). Ensure a file `peptides.txt` (generated by dna_processing.py) is present. Run `python3 clustering.py` to obtain cluster_consensus.xlsx, peptide_cluster.xlsx, and the align folder with MSAs and HMM profiles.

steps.title: Characterize gPhage library
steps.instruction: Determine the number of unique inserts and average insert size from NGS data (e.g., 2.2 × 10⁵ reads, 99 % unique, average 143 bp). Calculate the percentage of transformants containing T. cruzi inserts (e.g., 75 % of ~4 × 10⁸ colonies ≈ 3 × 10⁸ inserts). Compute library coverage (total insert bp ÷ haploid genome size ≈ 1.4 × 10³‑fold). Note that only ~17.8 % of inserts encode a peptide and ~8.9 % of those share ≥60 % similarity with a T. cruzi protein due to blunt‑end cloning in all frames.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze experimental results with GraphPad Prism 6; use Student’s t‑test to compare test phage particles against controls.
